messages.subject: longitudinal data
parts:
Dear INLA-community,

I am trying to fit a hierarchical model to longitudinal data, where 3 big groups would be located on the top of a heirarchy and be composed out of 25 smaller groups lying on the level beneath. The attached code produces random slopes for 3 big groups, indicating that each group reacted to 10 Time periods differently. This is shown in the attached Figure below: 

formula <-
  Y ~ 1 + f(smallgroup, time, model = "iid") + f(biggroup,  time, model = "iid")


model <- inla(formula,
              data = data, family = "T", control.family=list
              (hyper=list(dof=list(initial=1,fixed=T))),                      
              control.predictor=list(link=1, compute=TRUE))


The question is the following:

What if my primary interest is not on the random slopes, but on how each of 10 Time periods affected each big group? In other words, I am looking for the posterior predictive intervals for each Time period, like the ones I made up below in the attached Figures:    






Could you guys suggest how the model has to look like so as to get posterior predictive intervals like the ones in the make-believe Figures?
